title: Fruit & Veg Market Stall
strapline: Weigh it, bag it, tot it up — 'lovely apples, who's next?' shouted across the market.
intent: A market stall is a busy, sociable job that pulls children into calling out, welcoming customers and taking turns to serve and be served.
Weighing produce on real scales and counting coins into a till give number a genuine, urgent purpose — how many apples, how much does that come to, what's your change.
Handling and naming real fruit and vegetables builds rich vocabulary and a curiosity about where food comes from and how it grows.
Bagging, sorting and arranging the stall is precise physical work that also invites children to classify by colour, size and kind.
The stall welcomes the produce of every family's kitchen — okra, plantain, pak choi, mango — so children see their own foods valued and named.
implementation: Be a demanding, chatty customer — ask for 'three of the reddest ones', change your mind, query the price — every wrinkle stretches the talk and the maths.
Put out real (or convincingly weighty) produce and real scales so weighing means something, and model the stallholder's patter: 'lovely and fresh today, what can I get you?'
Give every stall a price board, paper bags, a till and coins, and treat totting up the bill as genuine, shared counting.
Sort and restock together — all the round ones here, the leafy ones there — and name each item precisely as you handle it.
Visit a real greengrocer or market if you can, then watch which words and gestures the children carry back into the play.
Link the stall to growing wherever possible — what we picked from the garden goes on sale today.
key_questions: Can I have three of the reddest ones, please?
How much does that come to altogether?
Which is heavier — the marrow or the bag of apples?
Where shall we put all the round ones and all the leafy ones?
What's this one called, and do you know how it grows?

impact.text: Children weigh produce and count coins, giving number a genuine, urgent purpose.
Children call out, welcome customers and take turns to serve and be served.
Children handle and name real fruit and vegetables, growing vocabulary and curiosity about food.
Children sort and arrange the stall by colour, size and kind.
Children see their own family's foods valued and named — okra, plantain, pak choi, mango.

enhancements: Real (or convincingly weighty) produce and real scales so weighing means something.
A price board, paper bags, a till and coins for totting up the bill.
A visit to a real greengrocer or market, then watching the words the children carry back.
A link to the garden — what was picked today goes on sale.
Foods from every family's kitchen, named and celebrated.

playing_exploring: Children step into a bustling grown-up world they have watched from a buggy, and the props pull them straight in.
Real scales and real weight invite genuine testing — which bag tips the balance, how many make it heavy.
active_learning: Running the stall means holding several jobs at once — serving, weighing, taking money — and children stay with the busyness because it matters.
creating_thinking: Children invent prices, special offers and solutions — what do we do when two customers both want the last cabbage?
